case.title: Default and saved settings show as separate groups in the reports
case.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • About 15 minutes today, plus 5 minutes the next day (the reports are not live).
  • Sign in on the QA branch (sv10043) with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List).
  • Work in one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"). To change it: your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  • Google Analytics: you can open the analytics property the QA build sends to (QA and staging share it) (Admin > DebugView shows each event within seconds, because the QA build sends in debug mode) and the Story 12 reports Milos Vasic builds there. If you cannot open DebugView, write "not checked by hand" for the event checks and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  • Events to look for in Google Analytics > Admin > DebugView: work_orders_display_view, work_orders_field_load, work_orders_density_load. Each shows a source: default (never changed) or saved (chosen earlier).

Setup

  1. Settings > Staff: add a brand-new user "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie" at this location with a role that has Work Orders View, and finish the invite so they can sign in. Do not open Work Orders as this user yet. If that name has been used before, add a new user and read the expected results with the new name.
  2. As Admin (the dispatcher): Work Orders > Board View > Density > pick Comfortable. Then sign out.
case.custom_steps:
1. Sign in as ZZAUTOTEST Newbie, open Work Orders and click Board View. In DebugView, read the source on the display, field and density events.
  2. Sign out, sign in as Admin, open Work Orders and click Board View. Read the same sources in DebugView.
  3. The next day, open the Story 12 density and field reports for the test date.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the events show source default.
  • Step 2: the density event shows source saved (Comfortable).
  • Step 3: the reports show default, saved and fallback as separate groups, with ZZAUTOTEST Newbie under default and your dispatcher's density under saved.
  • A fallback (a setting that could not be loaded) cannot be caused by hand. Write "fallback: not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10593 (Story 12, Google Analytics for display and field usage); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S12-R12, Story 12 report owner, read 8 Oct 2026. Event names and timing: SV-10593 comments by Slavcho Mitrov and Milos Vasic, 6 Oct 2026 (the agreed GA4 event table); earlier event contract on Review Decisions page 853901313 (29 Sep 2026) uses older names.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R12: “Separate default, saved, and fallback preference cohorts in reports.”
  • Story 12 report owner: “Milos Vasic owns building and maintaining the reports in S12-R4 and S12-R10 to S12-R12. Engineering’s part of this story ends at sending the events; Story 12 is complete when both are done.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

changes.label: Preconditions
changes.old_value:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. On the Work Orders QA build with Google Analytics enabled for the org and a way to observe the events fired (browser devtools Network tab, or engineering/dev support).
  4. Ensure the location has eligible lead technicians and work orders so the displays and fields can be exercised.
  5. Access to the analytics report output.
changes.new_value:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a dispatcher whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > on the Work Orders card, View and Create & Edit are both ticked. The Admin role has both).
  2. In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  3. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
  4. You can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  5. Event names to look for in DebugView: work_orders_display_view (a display was shown), work_orders_field_load and work_orders_density_load (the fields and density you have, once per display per session), work_orders_field_toggle and work_orders_density_change (a saved change).
  6. A brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders (Settings > Staff > add, e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie", with Work Orders View).
  7. Your dispatcher has chosen a density (e.g. Comfortable) in an earlier session.
  8. You can open the Story 12 reports in Google Analytics (built and kept by Milos Vasic).

changes.old_value:

  2. Confirm default, saved, and fallback preference cohorts are reported separately.
  3. Confirm the product defaults are not changed automatically based on the analytics.

  3. The next day (reports are not live), open the Story 12 reports and find the density and field reports for the test date.

Preconditions

  • Needs: 2 users · 1 browser · Google Analytics DebugView and Story 12 reports access · about 15 minutes plus a check the next day
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Analytics access: you can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  • Event names to look for in DebugView: work_orders_display_view (a display was shown), work_orders_field_load and work_orders_density_load (the fields and density you have, once per display per session), work_orders_field_toggle and work_orders_density_change (a saved change).
  • [User-B]: a brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders, "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie" (the expected results name this user), with Work Orders View.
  • Your dispatcher has chosen a density (e.g. Comfortable) in an earlier session.
  • You can open the Story 12 reports in Google Analytics (built and kept by Milos Vasic).

Setup

  1. Settings > Staff > add "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie" with a role that has Work Orders View, at this location, and finish the invite so the user can sign in. Do not open Work Orders as this user before step 1. If "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie" has already opened Work Orders (an earlier run), add a new user instead and read the expected results with that name.
  2. As your dispatcher, open Work Orders > Board View > Density and pick a value (e.g. Comfortable); then sign out so the next sign-in is a new session.
  3. Check the setup worked: Google Analytics > Admin > DebugView opens and shows your device within a few seconds of opening any ShopView page. If it does not, carry on but write "not checked by hand" for the event checks, as the Preconditions say.
